cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: The {{c1::parotid papilla}} is a small elevation on the buccal mucosa opposite the {{c2::maxillary second molars}}.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: The parotid papilla is the opening of {{c1::Stensen's}} duct, from the {{c2::parotid}} gland.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: The {{c1::maxillary tuberosity}} is the elevation behind the most posterior maxillary molar.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: The {{c1::retromolar pad}} is a dense pad behind the most posterior {{c2::mandibular}} molar.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: The {{c1::vestibule}} is the {{c2::horseshoe}}-shaped space between the cheeks, lips, and teeth.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: The {{c1::mucobuccal fold}} is the line where the {{c2::buccal}} mucosa meets the {{c3::alveolar}} mucosa.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: The {{c1::labial frenum}} is a vertical band that attaches the cheeks and lips to the alveolar mucosa.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: {{c1::Alveolar mucosa}} is the redder, thinner mucosa overlying the bone that can be stretched easily.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: {{c1::Attached gingiva}} is the thick band of gingiva bound to the tooth and the alveolar bone of the jaws; it may show areas of {{c2::pigmentation}}.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: {{c1::Marginal (free)}} gingiva is the non-attached gingiva towards the crown of the tooth.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: {{c1::Interdental}} gingiva is the gingival papilla between the teeth.

cloze.section: Oral vestibule, gingiva, and surrounding structures
cloze.text: The {{c1::mucogingival junction (MGJ)}} is the line where the {{c2::attached gingiva}} meets the {{c3::alveolar mucosa}}.
The {{c1::hard}} palate is the firmer, whiter {{c2::anterior}} part of the palate.
The {{c1::soft}} palate is the yellower, smaller, softer {{c2::posterior}} part of the palate.
The {{c1::incisive papilla}} is the small bulge on the palate just behind the {{c2::maxillary incisors}}.
The {{c1::palatine rugae}} are firm, irregular wave-like ridges of tissue on the surface of the (hard) palate.
The {{c1::palatine raphe}} is the prominent midline of the palate running from the {{c2::uvula}} to the {{c3::incisive papilla}}.
The palatine raphe is evidence of the {{c1::fusion of the palatal processes}} during fetal development.
The {{c1::uvula}} is the projection from the posterior edge of the soft palate.
The {{c1::pterygomandibular fold}} runs from the junction of the hard and soft palate on each side down to the mandible, just posterior to the most distal mandibular molar.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: The base of the tongue is the {{c1::posterior one-third}}; the body of the tongue is the {{c2::anterior two-thirds}}.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: The {{c1::dorsal}} surface of the tongue is the top surface; the {{c2::ventral}} surface is the bottom surface.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: The {{c1::lateral}} surfaces of the tongue are its sides.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: {{c1::Filiform}} papillae are the most numerous papillae on the dorsal surface of the tongue.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: Filiform papillae contain {{c1::tactile receptors}} but no {{c2::taste buds}}.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: Filiform papillae are missing in the area of {{c1::median rhomboid glossitis}}.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: {{c1::Fungiform}} papillae are mushroom-shaped papillae that appear as {{c2::red dots}} on the tongue.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: {{c1::Circumvallate}} papillae are the large papillae lined up along the {{c2::sulcus terminalis}}.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: There are {{c1::10–14}} circumvallate papillae, each containing over {{c2::100}} taste buds.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: Besides taste, circumvallate papillae help detect {{c1::temperature and touch}}.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: {{c1::Foliate}} papillae are the papillae on the {{c2::sides}} of the tongue.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: {{c1::Lingual papillae}} is the general term for all papillae on the tongue.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: The {{c1::sulcus terminalis}} is the {{c2::V}}-shaped groove separating the {{c3::body and base}} of the tongue.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: The {{c1::foramen cecum}} is the depression in the midline of the tongue at the V-shaped groove (sulcus terminalis).

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: The {{c1::lingual tonsil}} is the irregular mass of lymphoid tissue on the far back of the tongue, posterior to the {{c2::circumvallate papillae}}.
cloze.extra: The book describes it as paired (it is bilateral, on each side of the midline of the tongue base).

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: The {{c1::lingual frenum}} is the band of tissue between the ventral side of the tongue and the floor of the mouth.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: The {{c1::sublingual caruncle}} is the duct opening for the {{c2::submandibular}} and {{c2::sublingual}} salivary glands.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: {{c1::Lingual veins}} (lingual varicosities) are dark veins on the ventral surface of the tongue, more visible in {{c2::elderly}} patients.

cloze.section: Tongue and floor of the mouth
cloze.text: The {{c1::plica fimbriata}} is the bilateral fold next to the lingual veins on the ventral tongue.
The {{c1::pharynx}} (throat) is a muscular tube that serves as both {{c2::respiratory}} and {{c2::digestive}} tract.
The {{c1::nasopharynx}} is the part of the pharynx superior to the {{c2::soft palate}}, continuous with the nasal cavity.
cloze.extra: Book says it 'contains the nasal cavity'; more precisely it lies behind and is continuous with the nasal cavity.

cloze.text: The {{c1::oropharynx}} is the part of the pharynx between the {{c2::soft palate}} and the opening of the larynx.
cloze.extra: Book: 'between the soft palate and the opening of the pharynx'. The oropharynx extends from the soft palate down to the epiglottis/laryngeal opening.

cloze.text: The {{c1::laryngopharynx}} is the part of the pharynx below the oropharynx; it is {{c2::not visible}} during an intraoral examination.
The {{c1::epiglottis}} is the flap of cartilage below the base of the tongue, in front of the oropharynx.
The epiglottis stays {{c1::vertical}} at rest and covers the entrance of the {{c2::larynx}} during swallowing to prevent {{c3::aspiration}}.
The {{c1::faucial pillars}} are vertical folds of muscle surrounding the {{c2::palatine tonsils}}.
The anterior faucial pillar is formed by the {{c1::palatoglossus}} muscle.
The posterior faucial pillar is formed by the {{c1::palatopharyngeus}} muscle.
The {{c1::sternocleidomastoid}} muscle (SCM) is the large muscle on each side of the neck.
The {{c1::hyoid bone}} is suspended in the neck, {{c2::superior}} to the thyroid cartilage.
cloze.extra: It is the only bone not articulating with another bone.

cloze.text: The {{c1::thyroid cartilage}} ("Adam's apple") lies {{c2::superior}} to the thyroid gland.
The thyroid gland is {{c1::butterfly}}-shaped.
There are {{c1::4}} parathyroid glands, located on the (posterior) thyroid gland.
cloze.extra: Book: the thyroid gland 'contains 4 parathyroid glands'.

cloze.text: The {{c1::palatine tonsils}} lie between the anterior (palatoglossal) and posterior ({{c2::palatopharyngeal}}) faucial pillars.
cloze.extra: Book: 'between the palatopharyngeal muscles'.

cloze.text: In anatomic position the body stands tall with arms at the sides, {{c1::palms}} and toes facing forward.
In anatomic description, "right" and "left" refer to the {{c1::patient's}} right and left, not the clinician's.
A {{c1::sagittal}} plane is a vertical plane that divides the body into {{c2::right and left}} parts.
The {{c1::median (midsagittal)}} plane divides the body into {{c2::equal}} right and left halves.
The {{c1::frontal (coronal)}} plane is a vertical plane that divides the body into {{c2::front and back}}.
The {{c1::horizontal (transverse)}} plane divides the body into {{c2::upper and lower}} portions, perpendicular to the long axis of the body.
Skeletal function — {{c1::support}}: bones form a rigid framework giving the body its shape (e.g., cervical vertebrae support the head).
cloze.extra: Like poles supporting a tent.

cloze.text: Skeletal function — {{c1::protection}}: e.g., the {{c2::cranium}} protects the brain and the eye sockets shield the eyeballs.
cloze.extra: Skin is the first barrier; bones defend vital internal structures.

cloze.text: Skeletal function — {{c1::movement}}: bones act as {{c2::levers}} for muscles (e.g., the mandible moves at the TMJ for chewing and speaking).
Skeletal function — {{c1::blood production}}: bone {{c2::marrow}} makes red and white blood cells.
cloze.extra: WBCs are critical for healing, inflammation, and defense during periodontitis.

cloze.text: Skeletal function — {{c1::mineral storage}}: bones store {{c2::calcium}} and {{c2::phosphorus}}.
cloze.extra: Supports teeth, bone repair, and muscle contraction.

cloze.text: The skull has {{c1::22}} bones; the whole body has {{c2::206}}.
There are {{c1::8}} cranial bones and {{c2::14}} facial bones.
The 8 cranial bones: frontal ({{c1::1}}), parietal ({{c2::2}}), temporal ({{c3::2}}), occipital (1), sphenoid (1), ethmoid (1).
cloze.extra: Paired cranial bones: parietal and temporal only.

cloze.text: Of the cranial bones, the {{c1::frontal}}, {{c1::occipital}}, {{c1::sphenoid}} and {{c1::ethmoid}} are single (unpaired).
The 14 facial bones: maxillae (2), mandible (1), zygomatic (2), nasal (2), lacrimal (2), palatine (2), inferior nasal conchae (2), {{c1::vomer}} (1).
The only two unpaired facial bones are the {{c1::mandible}} and the {{c1::vomer}}.
The skull houses {{c1::foramina}} for nerves and vessels (e.g., mental, infraorbital, mandibular).
The skull forms spaces such as the {{c1::orbit}}, {{c1::nasal cavity}}, and {{c1::oral cavity}}.
A bony {{c1::process}} is a projection on a bony surface.
The {{c1::coronoid}} process of the mandible is the thin, pointed process where the {{c2::temporalis}} muscle inserts; it assists jaw {{c3::elevation}}.
A {{c1::condyle}} is an oval projection usually involved in {{c2::joints}}.
The mandibular condyle fits into the {{c1::temporal}} bone to form the {{c2::TMJ}}.
A bony {{c1::head}} is a rounded bony surface supported by a {{c2::neck}} (e.g., the head of the mandibular condyle).
A {{c1::tuberosity}} is a rough area that provides muscle or tendon attachment.
The maxillary tuberosity, behind the last upper molar, anchors part of the {{c1::medial pterygoid}} muscle.
A {{c1::cornu}} is a horn-like projection (e.g., the greater cornu of the {{c2::hyoid}} bone, an attachment site for neck muscles).
A {{c1::tubercle}} is a small, rounded elevation.
The tubercle of the upper lip is the bump at the center of the {{c1::vermilion border}}.
A {{c1::crest}} is a prominent ridge on a bone.
The {{c1::alveolar crest}} is the top edge of the bone between two teeth.
cloze.extra: Like a ridge between mountain peaks.

cloze.text: A bony {{c1::ridge}} is a linear raised area.
The {{c1::internal oblique ridge}} is on the inner surface of the mandible and marks the {{c2::mylohyoid}} attachment.
cloze.extra: Also called the mylohyoid line.

cloze.text: A bony {{c1::spine}} is a pointed bony projection.
The {{c1::anterior nasal spine}} is found at the base of the nasal cavity and can appear on radiographs.
A {{c1::notch}} is a curved indentation along a bone.
The mandibular notch lies between the {{c1::coronoid}} and {{c1::condylar}} processes of the mandible.
A {{c1::sulcus}} is a shallow groove that houses soft tissues.
The {{c1::infraorbital sulcus}} runs within the orbit and carries the infraorbital nerve and vessels.
A {{c1::fossa}} is a broad, deep depression in bone.
The {{c1::mandibular fossa}} of the {{c2::temporal}} bone receives the mandibular condyle to form the TMJ.
A {{c1::foramen}} is a small opening for nerves or vessels.
The {{c1::mental}} foramen is located near the mandibular {{c2::premolars}} and transmits the mental nerve.
A {{c1::canal}} is a long, narrow tunnel through bone.
The {{c1::mandibular canal}} runs inside the mandible and carries the {{c2::inferior alveolar}} nerve and vessels.
A {{c1::fissure}} is a narrow, slit-like opening in bone.
The {{c1::pterygomaxillary fissure}} is located behind the {{c2::maxilla}}.
cloze.extra: Book: visible in posterior radiographs (it is seen on lateral cephalometric and panoramic images).

cloze.text: A {{c1::suture}} is an immovable union between skull bones.
The {{c1::coronal}} suture connects the frontal bone with the paired {{c2::parietal}} bones.
A {{c1::joint}} is the site where two bones meet.
The temporomandibular joint connects the {{c1::mandible}} to the {{c1::temporal}} bone and allows jaw movement.
The {{c1::temporal}} bones are irregular bones on the sides of the skull above the ears, forming part of the cranial base and lateral walls.
cloze.extra: Tip: you massage this area when you have a headache.

cloze.text: The {{c1::articular (mandibular) fossa}} of the temporal bone is the shallow depression where the {{c2::mandibular condyle}} sits to form the TMJ.
cloze.extra: Tip: place your fingers in front of your ear and open your jaw to feel movement.

cloze.text: The {{c1::mastoid process}} is the rounded bump of the temporal bone behind the ear, for muscle attachment.
cloze.extra: Tip: the hard bump you feel behind your earlobe.

cloze.text: The {{c1::styloid process}} is the thin pointed projection of the temporal bone below the ear canal, anchoring muscles and ligaments of the {{c2::tongue and throat}}.
cloze.extra: Tip: think of it as a hidden hook deep under the ear.

cloze.text: The {{c1::external acoustic (auditory) meatus}} is the tunnel-like opening of the temporal bone leading into the ear canal.
cloze.extra: Tip: this is your ear hole.

cloze.text: The {{c1::zygomatic process}} of the temporal bone extends forward to form the cheek arch with the {{c2::zygomatic}} bone.
cloze.extra: Tip: trace it from your temple to your cheek.

cloze.text: The {{c1::temporalis}} muscle originates on the side of the skull (temporal region) and inserts on the {{c2::mandible}} (coronoid process) to help {{c3::close}} the jaw.
cloze.extra: Broad, fan-like muscle. Tip: clench your teeth and feel it bulge at your temple.

cloze.text: The {{c1::frontal}} bone is a broad, flat bone forming the forehead, the roof of the {{c2::orbits}}, and part of the nasal cavity.
cloze.extra: Tip: you touch this area when raising your eyebrows.

cloze.text: The {{c1::frontal eminences}} are smooth, rounded areas on the forehead, more prominent in {{c2::children}}.
cloze.extra: Tip: gently press your upper forehead — the soft bulges on each side.

cloze.text: The {{c1::supraorbital ridge}} is the bony ridge above each eye socket.
cloze.extra: Tip: just under your eyebrows — helps protect the eye.

cloze.text: The {{c1::supraorbital foramen (or notch)}} is a small opening or indentation in the upper orbital rim for nerve and vessels.
cloze.extra: Tip: target site for the supraorbital nerve block.

cloze.text: The {{c1::frontal sinus}} is an air-filled cavity inside the frontal bone above the orbits.
cloze.extra: Tip: can cause pain or pressure in the brow area when inflamed.

cloze.text: The paired {{c1::parietal}} bones are large, curved bones forming the upper sides and roof of the skull.
cloze.extra: Tip: place your hands flat on the top sides of your head.

cloze.text: The two parietal bones are joined at the midline by the {{c1::sagittal}} suture.
cloze.extra: Runs front to back along the top of the head like a seam.

cloze.text: The parietal bones border the {{c1::frontal}}, {{c1::temporal}}, and {{c1::occipital}} bones.
cloze.extra: These sutures are helpful orientation lines on radiographs.

cloze.text: The {{c1::occipital}} bone is the flat bone forming the back and base of the skull.
cloze.extra: Tip: the bone you press against a headrest when leaning back.

cloze.text: The {{c1::foramen magnum}} of the occipital bone is the large opening for the {{c2::spinal cord}}.
cloze.extra: The brainstem passes through here — a key anatomic landmark.

cloze.text: The {{c1::occipital condyles}} sit on the first cervical vertebra, the {{c2::atlas}}.
cloze.extra: They allow the head to nod up and down.

cloze.text: The {{c1::external occipital protuberance}} is the midline bump on the back of the skull.
cloze.extra: Tip: a firm bump you can feel at the base of the skull.

cloze.text: The {{c1::sphenoid}} bone is the {{c2::butterfly}}-shaped bone at the base of the skull behind the eyes.
cloze.extra: Hidden deep inside, it touches almost every other cranial bone.

cloze.text: The greater and lesser {{c1::wings}} of the sphenoid are lateral projections forming part of the {{c2::orbit}} and cranial floor.
cloze.extra: Visible on lateral cephalometric radiographs.

cloze.text: The {{c1::sella turcica}} of the sphenoid is the saddle-shaped depression that holds the {{c2::pituitary}} gland.
cloze.extra: A landmark on skull X-rays.
